html:
In January 1991 tens of thousands of Latvians built barricades of concrete blocks, trucks and tractors around parliament and other key buildings in Riga, to protect them from Soviet troops.

Latvia had declared its aim of independence in May 1990. After Soviet forces killed protesters in Vilnius on 13 January 1991, people across Latvia came to Riga to stand guard, warming themselves at bonfires. On 20 January Soviet special police attacked the Interior Ministry, and five people were killed.

The crackdown failed, and the Soviet Union backed off under world pressure. Latvia became fully independent in August 1991 after the failed coup in Moscow. The barricades are remembered as the moment the Singing Revolution faced force, as it did in Lithuania.
sum: In January 1991 tens of thousands of Latvians built barricades of concrete blocks, trucks and tractors around parliament and other key buildings in Riga, to protect them from Soviet troops.
